transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because my family keeps acting like I’m making things up. They keep pointing to bank papers and saying, “See, nothing was taken,” but those papers don’t prove anything to me. I’ve known for over a year that they’re hiding my money.

And it’s not just one thing—it’s the bills, then these fundraisers, then talking about trips like it’s all normal. People use “plans” to cover what they’re really doing, you know? My cousin did that once with a church raffle—well, not exactly the same, but it made me notice how people can make money disappear and everyone just smiles.

So I came because they want me to stop asking, but I can’t. I have to keep confronting them until somebody finally tells the truth.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you don't seem to notice or hear?

I don’t think so… I mean, I hear people talking when they’re talking, like in the house or on the phone, but not voices out of nowhere, if that’s what you mean.

Seeing things—no, not like seeing ghosts or something. I see the papers they show me, and the receipts, and then they act like I’m supposed to just accept it. But that’s not the same as seeing things that aren’t there. So… no, I haven’t noticed anything like that.

Over the past year, have you had any periods lasting a week or more where your mood was unusually elevated, irritable, or energetic, or alternatively, periods where you felt very depressed, lost interest in things, or had trouble sleeping or eating?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I get upset, but anybody would get upset when people keep telling you you’re wrong. A whole week of being, like, extra happy or full of energy… I don’t really know. I don’t keep track like that.

Sleep and eating, I guess some days are different, but I don’t know if it’s a “period” like you’re saying. My aunt used to write everything on a calendar—what she ate, who called, all of it—and maybe if I did that I could tell you better. But just sitting here, I haven’t noticed something like that clearly.
Have you had any recent head injuries, neurological problems, or medical illnesses, or do you use alcohol or any drugs, that started around the same time these beliefs began?

I don’t know… I mean, I didn’t hit my head or anything that I can remember. No hospital thing around then. People keep asking like maybe there’s some other reason, but that’s not really what started it.

I don’t really do drugs. Alcohol… not really, maybe if somebody has something at a party, but I don’t keep track of that. My uncle used to say people blame drinking when they don’t want to talk about money, and that kind of stuck with me. But no, I can’t point to some injury or sickness starting the same time.
Since these beliefs started, have you noticed any changes in your ability to keep up with work, take care of yourself day-to-day, or stay connected with friends and family?

I mean… aside from the fights about the money, I still do my regular things. I make my own food, I get myself to the county clinic and the assistance appointments when I’m supposed to. I keep my stuff in order, my papers and clothes and all that, same as before.

People act like if I’m upset then I must not be handling things, but that’s not really true. My cousin’s place was always a mess, and nobody said anything about him, you know? But with me, they look at one argument and make it into something bigger. But day to day, I’m still taking care of what I need to.
Have others told you that your speech or behavior seems confusing or hard to follow, or have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy or feeling emotionally 'flat'?

I don’t think so… I mean, people say I “go on and on,” but that’s usually when they don’t want to hear the whole story. Like my sister will cut me off after two sentences, and then later she says I didn’t explain it right, but how can I explain if she’s already walking into the kitchen?

Hard to follow… maybe if they’re not listening. I still like things, I guess. I don’t know about “flat.” Some days I’m just tired of talking about the same arguments. My aunt used to sit with the TV on and not say a word for hours, and everybody called that peaceful, but if I’m quiet then suddenly it’s a problem. So… no, I haven’t really noticed that like you’re saying.

Aside from the situation with your family and the money, do you have similar strong suspicions or beliefs that other people—like coworkers, neighbors, or people you don't know well—are trying to deceive or harm you?

Not really like strangers, no… it’s mostly the people close enough to get into it, you know? My family, and some friends who say the bank papers prove nothing was taken. But papers can be made to look a certain way. For over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money, and then there’s always some bill or fundraiser or trip plan that pops up right when I ask about it.

So I have to keep bringing it up, because if I stop, then they just get to act like nothing happened. It’s not like I walk around thinking every neighbor is after me. It’s them, the ones who know the truth and won’t say it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, fixed, non-bizarre delusional belief—that family members are hiding/stealing money—persisting for over one year. The delusion is encapsulated (limited to close family, not generalized suspicion of strangers) and is reinforced by idiosyncratic but non-bizarre reasoning (misinterpreting bills, fundraisers, and trips as 'cover'). There are no hallucinations, no thought disorder or disorganized speech, no negative symptoms (flat affect, anhedonia), and no manic or depressive episodes meeting criteria for a mood disorder. Daily functioning (self-care, appointments, household tasks) remains intact aside from conflict specifically related to the delusional content. No substance use or medical/neurological cause identified. This clinical picture—an isolated, persistent, non-bizarre delusion without prominent hallucinations, mood episodes, or functional decline—is most consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22), rather than Schizophrenia (which requires additional psychotic symptoms such as hallucinations, disorganization, or negative symptoms) or a Mood Disorder with psychotic features (no manic/depressive episode identified).
